newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch start mass pig cull to contain swine fever.
newsitem.headline: Dutch start mass pig cull to contain swine fever.

text.p: The Netherlands will begin the slaughter of 30,000 pigs on Monday in a bid to contain a swine fever outbreak that has spread to 11 farms in the south of the country in the space of a week, the Farm Ministry said.
"The pigs will be killed at a location at the centre of the outbreak," a spokeswoman said.
Swine fever, last detected in the Netherlands in 1992, is highly contagious, although it is not harmful to humans.

The Dutch authorities, anxious to prevent restrictions on key pork exports, have decided to slaughter all pigs at 26 farms in the area surrounding the unit where the first case was discovered last Tuesday.
They have designated a wider area of some 600 square kilometres within which the transport of all manure and livestock, apart from poultry, has been banned.
Dutch Agriculture Minister Jozias van Aartsen visited the region over the weekend to oversee the containment measures.
"We have the situation in hand," he told Dutch television.
The Netherlands exports around 750,000 tonnes of pigs and pork products each year.
On Friday, Poland closed its borders to all imports of Dutch pigs, pork and pork products.
Belgium said it would tighten frontier checks, but stopped short of an outright ban.
"The only country that has banned imports so far is Poland. Belgium has announced restrictions but you can still export pigs to Belgium," the spokeswoman added.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture said on Friday it was closely monitoring developments and would make a decision this week on what action it should take.
A USDA official said the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service was watching to see if the Dutch government was taking adequate measures to "successfully control the situation".
The outbreak has so far been confined to a relatively small area in the province of North Brabant, and the government hopes its strategy will be enough to contain the disease.

The ban on the transport of livestock covers an area that exceeds European Union disease management regulations, which stipulate a transport embargo within a 10 kilometre radius of the centre of an outbreak, the farm ministry said.
"This is a very dangerous disease and it can spread very quickly, but we're hoping it has been contained," a spokeswoman said on Thursday.
The EU's Standing Veterinary Committee will hold a special meeting on Wednesday to discuss swine fever, focusing on the Netherlands and Germany, where there is also a serious outbreak.
Germany last week prohibited the export of pigs for slaughter from four German states and ordered the destruction of over 14,000 pigs.
Belgium and Switzerland have already announced restrictions on imports from Germany of live pigs and pork meat.
